_doc: Revert-verify mutants for ems__Bug 530f895d — the comparison sites of property_append / property_replace go through `listItemIdentity` (a wikilink is identified by its link target), the #4432 no-op refusal stays BYTE-based, and the write side stays verbatim. One mutant per decision, each must redden exactly its axes. Run from the repo root: python3 -I ~/.claude/bin/mutant-driver.py <this file> after setting `tree` and `subject` to YOUR checkout (both absolute). Sibling spec `wikilink-identity-530f895d.identity.spec.json` mutates the identity function itself (subject yamlScalar.ts — the driver takes one subject per spec). M1/M2/M4 put one comparison site back on whole-string comparison; M3 puts the refusal on identity (the StageSpecification design rejected in review of PR #4563); M8 removes the byte refusal (#4432); M5/M6/M11 lock the WRITE side (`to`, the appended value and the co-values are written as passed / as stored); M7 locks identity on BOTH sides of the `to` comparison; M9 locks the exact-match-first `from` lookup; M10 locks the `i !== fromIndex` exclusion; M12 locks the identity no-op refusal (a `from` found by link target whose stored item already equals `to`); M13 locks the refusal text naming the stored form.
subject: <ABSOLUTE PATH TO YOUR exocortex CHECKOUT>/packages/core/src/services/GroundingExecutor.ts

M1_append_dedup_by_string._note: property_append dedup compares whole strings again: the class present in the other form is written a second time.

M2_replace_from_by_string._note: property_replace looks `from` up by whole string again (the identity fallback degenerates to the exact lookup) — the reported defect: refusal on the aliased form.

M3_same_value_by_identity._note: The #4432 no-op refusal compares link-target identities instead of bytes (the StageSpecification design): rewriting ONE target's alias is refused, so a wrong alias can no longer be repaired (review MEDIUM-1 of PR #4563 — NoteToRDFConverter reads the alias first, so the rewrite is a real change) and a two-form duplicate cannot be collapsed.

M4_replace_to_present_by_string._note: property_replace does not see `to` already present in the other form — writes the class a second time (grooming facet (a)).

M5_replace_writes_identity._note: D3 — property_replace writes the IDENTITY of `to` instead of `to` as passed: an aliased `to` loses its alias on disk.

M6_append_writes_identity._note: D3 — property_append writes the IDENTITY of the value instead of the value as passed: an aliased class loses its alias on disk.

M7_to_present_vs_raw_to._note: `to already present` compares the item's identity with the RAW `to`: an aliased `to` misses its plain form on disk (and a two-form duplicate is no longer collapsible).

M8_byte_identical_refusal_removed._note: #4432 — byte-identical `from === to` is accepted again: with the value twice in the list the identity no-op guard refuses it under the wrong reason (K21), and a pair matching the stored item only by link target rewrites the alias away and reports success (K28). Same mutation as M10 of property-replace-02de55a4.executor.spec.json, locked here on this suite's own axes.

M9_no_exact_first._note: the exact-spelling lookup of `from` is skipped: the FIRST form of the target is replaced instead of the item `from` names.

M10_to_present_includes_from._note: `to already present` no longer excludes the `from` item: rewriting one target's alias finds `from` itself as `to` and DELETES the value (review LOW-4 of PR #4563 — the term became load-bearing with identity comparison). Type-preserving: `i` stays used.

M11_replace_rewrites_co_values._note: D3 — property_replace rewrites the co-values into their identity form: their aliases are stripped on disk.

M12_identity_noop_refusal_removed._note: Review round 2 of PR #4563 — the guard against the #4432 no-op reached through the identity lookup is removed: `from` matched a stored item by link target that already equals `to`, the map branch rewrites it with itself and the command reports a replacement on a byte-identical file.

M13_stored_form_not_named._note: Review round 2 of PR #4563 (LOW-3) — a byte-identical pair that matched the stored item only by link target gets the generic "can only leave unchanged" refusal, which is false there (the stored form differs) and hides which `from` to pass.
